candidates.exact_span: In addition, if the State amends a TMDL, this permit may be reopened to establish effluent limitations for the parameter(s) to be consistent with that TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether effluent limitations tied to a TMDL are already enforceable numeric limits in the current permit term, or only become applicable after a reopening, would change which discharge limits are in force during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permit may be reopened and modified during the life of the permit if State Water Quality Standards are promulgated or revised.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If revised or newly promulgated State Water Quality Standards are interpreted as immediately altering applicable limits versus only taking effect upon permit reopening, the numeric limits used for FY2025 compliance comparisons could differ.

candidates.exact_span: The facility had TRC violation in March 2019, November 2019, January 2020, October 2020, and December 2020.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage identifies TRC as a parameter subject to enforceable permit limits; interpreting whether the same TRC limit regime carries forward into the reissued permit term affects which numeric limit applies to FY2025 TRC measurements.

candidates.exact_span: A review of the DMR during the last permit cycle revealed that the facility was in violations of its permit for nine quarters (from the first quarter of 2016 to the first quarter of 2021).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reference to DMR review during the prior permit cycle bears on whether routine DMR submission and associated monitoring parameters were required obligations that continue under the reissued permit covering FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee cited the reason for the November excursion is due to no flow in the irrigation ditch that the backwash water flows into.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether backwash discharge with no irrigation-ditch flow triggers, suspends, or alters monitoring obligations and how such a no-flow condition is documented affects both applicability of discharge-dependent monitoring requirements and classification of related missing or excursion evidence.

candidates.exact_span: With no flow of irrigation water, the facility believes that its backwash water did reach the receiving stream.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether backwash water is treated as having reached the receiving stream under no-flow conditions (including possible misreading of 'did' versus 'did not') changes whether a discharge is deemed to have occurred, which in turn affects conditional monitoring applicability and whether periods should be classified as no-discharge, documented no-data, or unresolved missing evidence.
